traits: Cap 3 to 7 cm, convex without being pointed, then spreading with a slight boss; from pure pink to violet or grey, it whitens in dry weather; very thin margin, striate from the gills
Unequal, fairly distant gills, whitish to pinkish
Stem 4 to 9 cm, the colour of the cap or more violet, slightly striate, fragile, hollow
White flesh · clear smell and taste of radish
Common from spring to autumn, under broadleaves and conifers
safetyNote: Toxic: it contains muscarine, which causes the sweating syndrome: heavy sweating, tears and salivation, short breath, nausea and vomiting, within minutes to 2 hours (Belgian poison centre). The German mycological society lists Mycena pura and Mycena rosea among muscarine mushrooms; M. rosea is often only a variety of M. pura. In 2022, pickers looking for amethyst deceivers picked mycenas (ANSES). The deceiver has more distant gills, a hard stem and no smell of radish.
